newsitem.title: USA: TABLE - HFS Inc Q2 net shr loss $0.57.
newsitem.headline: TABLE - HFS Inc Q2 net shr loss $0.57.

text.p: NOTES: Financial data above excludes a second quarter 1997 one-time charge related to the PHH merger of $303 million ($277 million after tax, or $1.26 per share)
(1) Historical financial results have been restated for all periods presented to include the financial results of PHH Corporation, which was acquired via pooling of interests on April 30, 1997.

(2) Pro Forma financial results reflect 1996 financial information assuming that the acquisitions of Travelodge, Electronic Realty Associates, Century 21 Non-Owned Regions, Coldwell Banker, Avis Inc., Resort Condominiums International and PHH Corporation were completed on January 1, 1996.
(3) Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation and Amortization.

(4) Earnings Per Share is presented on a fully diluted basis which for second quarter ended June 30, 1997 and June 30, 1996, assume that the $150 million 4 1/2% Convertible Notes are converted into 8.2 million common shares. After-tax interest expense of $1.1 million related to these Convertible Notes are added back to net income for the respective periods in computing fully diluted earnings per share. Additionally, earnings per share, for the second quarter ended June 30, 1997 assumes the $240 million 4 3/4% Convertible Notes are converted into 3.6 million common shares. After-tax interest expense of $1.8 million related to these Convertible Notes are added back to net income for the quarter ended June 30, 1997 in computing fully diluted earnings per share.

(5) Earnings Per Share is presented on a fully diluted basis which for six months ended June 30, 1997 and June 30, 1996, assume that the $150 million 4 1/2% Convertible Notes are converted into 8.2 million common shares. After-tax interest expense of $2.1 million related to these Convertible Notes are added back to net income for the respective periods in computing fully diluted earnings per share. Additionally, earnings per share, for the six months ended June 30, 1997 assumes the $240 million 4 3/4% Convertible Notes are converted into 3.6 million common shares. After-tax interest expense of $3.6 million related to these Convertible Notes are added back to net income for the quarter ended June 30, 1997 in computing fully diluted earnings per share.

(6) Adjusted earnings per share represents the cash earnings per share of the company and is computed by adding the company's depreciation and amortization to net income available to common shareholders, less maintenance capital expenditures. This numerator is then divided by average shares outstanding on a fully diluted basis.
